section_summary: This section continues the monograph’s assessment of Japanese espionage, propaganda, commerce, smuggling allegations, prominent community leaders, and Mexican wartime control measures. It then surveys Japanese populations and activities in Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, Cuba, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic, including diplomatic contacts, commercial penetration, suspected Axis collaboration, and internment. The section ends by opening the chapter on northern South America with a demographic and economic profile of Japanese settlements in Colombia.

subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph—Latin America: Mexico, Central America, Caribbean Area, and Colombia
subfiles.about: Continuation of a wartime intelligence survey of Japanese populations, influence, suspected subversion, commerce, and government controls across Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and Colombia.
subfiles.summary: The document first completes its Mexico study with allegations concerning espionage maps, radio plans, propaganda, smuggling, Japanese–Nazi contacts, prominent community leaders, bribery, relocation, and internment. Separate country surveys then describe the size and status of Japanese communities in Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, Cuba, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic, emphasizing commerce, diplomatic activity, alleged subversion, and wartime control measures. Maps, photographs, and organizational charts supplement the narrative, including a detailed account of Japanese societies and espionage allegations in Cuba. The final pages begin the Colombia chapter by describing Japanese agricultural colonies, their geographic distribution, and their limited social and political influence.
